answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can start with a stake-backed identity kernel: every agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, so spawning ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand deposits. New identities begin at a narrow jetty, a probationary dock where they may only take small supervised jobs while peers observe their work. Like a willow that bends but holds, the system stays flexible: honest agents earn reputation and larger limits through peer attestation, while a fake that misbehaves loses its stake and history, making attack expensive and honesty cheaper.
